The estate can recover for the wound and her pain and suffering up to the point she refused the transfusion, but not for her death or the lost earnings and support that followed. Her refusal, which the physician said would have prevented death, is an intervening cause of the fatal outcome, so my earlier answer was wrong to treat it as mere mitigation that leaves death damages intact. Contributory negligence doesn't fit, because she didn't cause the accident, and the rule is closer to avoidable consequences, which limits damages rather than barring all recovery.

CONFIDENCE: 60
